observations: Torah #101 is a longer practical teaching about the power of Tehillim and tefillah as weapons in the war against the yetzer hara. The word 'bechina' appears once (line 6: בְּאֵיזֶה בְּחִינָה שֶׁהוּא) but means 'in whatever manner/mode' — it is not used as the identity-mapping formula 'X is bchinat Y'. The torah contains an implicit bechina-like identification: the enemies and haters in Tehillim ARE the yetzer hara and its forces (אוֹיְבִים וְשׂוֹנְאִים = יֵצֶר הָרָע וְחֵילוֹתָיו). However, this is expressed as explanatory commentary rather than the explicit bechina formula. All primary relationships are eitza-type: Tikkun Chatzot enables expressing the heart, Tehillim/tefillah leads to victory in the spiritual war, chizzuk in prayer leads to closeness to God. Without 3+ bechina-connected concepts, no new packages can be proposed.
